content: For the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults, the recommended dosage of quinine sulfate is 648 mg, which is equivalent to two capsules, taken orally every 8 hours for a duration of 7 days. It is advised to take QUALAQUIN with food to reduce the likelihood of gastric discomfort. In patients with acute uncomplicated malaria who also have severe chronic renal impairment, the recommended dosing regimen begins with a loading dose of 648 mg of QUALAQUIN. This is followed 12 hours later by maintenance doses of 324 mg administered every 12 hours. The effects of mild to moderate renal impairment on the safety and pharmacokinetics of quinine sulfate have not been established. For patients with mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment, no adjustment to the recommended dose is necessary. However, these patients should be closely monitored for potential adverse effects associated with quinine. Quinine should not be administered to patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).
